summary: Deploy the new version with a state-only migration, retire the old version, then add a unique constraint on last_name after the old version retires. This avoids altering pre-existing last_name values while achieving the unique constraint goal once only the new version serves traffic.
write_consistency: During the overlap, the old version serves traffic with unchanged last_name values; the new version enforces uniqueness at the ORM model level. After retire_old, the unique constraint is added to the database, ensuring DB-level uniqueness alongside application-level enforcement.
revision_notes: Fixed the add_unique_constraint SQL stage: removed the invalid NOT VALID keyword, which PostgreSQL does not support for UNIQUE constraints. The SQL statement is now `ALTER TABLE account_user ADD CONSTRAINT unique_last_name UNIQUE (last_name);`. This stage is positioned after retire_old per the rule that contract SQL stages must not run while the old version is still running.

stages.description: Retire the old version so only the new version continues.
Add a unique constraint on the last_name column after old version retirement.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD CONSTRAINT unique_last_name UNIQUE (last_name);
